svg.title: Row vs Column Storage
svg.desc: Row vs Column Storage. Store rows together for transactions or columns together for analytics, and why a column store scans and compresses so much faster. Step 1, A row store reads it all: PostgreSQL reads every page of whole rows, 82 MB, to use 19 of each row's 68 bytes: about 130 ms. Step 2, Store each column apart: DuckDB stores each column apart, bit-packed to 1 to 20 bits a value; the scan reads 3 of 5 columns. Step 3, Measured: 13× less data: Same 12 rows: DuckDB reads 6.25 MB instead of 82 MB and answers in about 5 ms instead of 130 ms. Step 4, One-row writes favour rows: One UPDATE: PostgreSQL writes a new row version; DuckDB's CHECKPOINT rewrites 122,880 qty values.

g.text: 1 · A row store reads it all
1 · A row store reads it all
PostgreSQL reads every page of whole rows, 82 MB, to use 19 of each row's 68 bytes: about 130 ms.
DuckDB stores each column apart, bit-packed to 1 to 20 bits a value; the scan reads 3 of 5 columns.
Same 12 rows: DuckDB reads 6.25 MB instead of 82 MB and answers in about 5 ms instead of 130 ms.
One UPDATE: PostgreSQL writes a new row version; DuckDB's CHECKPOINT rewrites 122,880 qty values.
SELECT p.category, sum(i.qty * i.price_thb) AS revenue
FROM order_items i JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY revenue DESC
UPDATE order_items SET qty = 3 WHERE order_id = 2 AND line_no = 1
× 1,250,000 rows = 81 MB read, 28% of it used
the 8 kB page is the unit of I/O, so every column comes along
Parallel Seq Scan: three processes share every page
+ the 94 pages of products, for the hash join
-> Parallel Seq Scan on order_items i
PostgreSQL 18.6: 10,417 pages of order_items + 94 of products = 82 MB
DuckDB 1.5.6: 25 blocks of 256 kB = 6.25 MB, both tables, same scale
PostgreSQL: each plan node hands up one row per call
DuckDB: each call carries a vector of up to 2,048 values
+ an entry (2,1) → (10416,81) in order_items_pkey: no room on page 0, so not HOT
DuckDB 1.5.6 · the qty segment of row group 0: 60 vectors, 122,880 values
WAL 147 B, then CHECKPOINT writes all 60 vectors again: 266,240 B
between them: CDC or batch ELT
Parallel Seq Scan on order_items → Hash Join → Partial HashAggregate
TABLE_SCAN product_id, qty, price_thb → HASH_JOIN → HASH_GROUP_BY
each column segment compressed on its own: DELTA_FOR (order_id), FOR bit-packing (the other four), dictionary (category)
zone maps: order_id 475,224–498,664 → 2 of 11 row groups
Index Scan on order_items_pkey: 4 pages, 32 kB
new version (10416,81) + index entry · WAL 3 records, 235 B
zone map → row group 0: 122,880 keys, 1 block of 256 kB
WAL 147 B; CHECKPOINT rewrites the segment: 266,240 B
